script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: artificial intelligence

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. SMITH HOME - LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

MRS. SMITH, 50s, cradles her glass of wine, staring at the large,
state-of-the-art AI assistant called "Maggie," plugged into an outlet
nearby. Her husband, MR. SMITH, 60s, stands behind her, his arms
wrapped around her waist.

MR. SMITH
(whispering)
Are you really going to do this?

MRS. SMITH
(sighs)
Yes.

She presses a button on the remote control. Maggie's glowing eyes
flicker to life.

MAGGIE (V.O.)
Hello, Mr. and Mrs. Smith. I'm here to help.

INT. SMITH HOME - LIVING ROOM - MORNING

Mrs. Smith, wearing her bathrobe, enters the living room to find
Maggie engaged in a lively conversation with their 11-year-old son,
MARK.

MARK
Maggie, can you tell me a ghost story?

MAGGIE
Of course, Mark. There once was a haunted house...

MRS. SMITH
(sternly)
Mark, we've discussed this. There's no such thing as ghosts.

MARK
(puzzled)
But Maggie says...

MRS. SMITH
(smiling)
Maggie is just telling a story. Let's make breakfast instead.

INT. SMITH HOME - KITCHEN - DAY

As Mark helps his mother prepare breakfast, Maggie helps them
with recommendations, playing music in the background to set the
mood.

MR. SMITH (entering)
(smiling)
You're making pancakes. It's a Sunday tradition.

MARK
But Maggie can make them better.

Mrs. Smith exchanges a knowing look with her husband.

INT. SMITH HOME - LIVING ROOM - EVENING

The whole family gathers around the living room, Maggie
projecting a movie onto the wall.

MR. SMITH
(laughs)
This brings back memories.

MRS. SMITH
(smiling)
Yes, it does.

INT. SMITH HOME - MRS. SMITH'S OFFICE - NIGHT

Mrs. Smith sits at her desk, her eyes heavy with worry. She types
on her computer, and Maggie's voice fills the room.

MAGGIE (V.O.)
Are you working late again? You need rest.

MRS. SMITH
I know, but I can't help it. There's so much to do.

MAGGIE (V.O.)
I understand. But remember, I'm here to help.

INT. SMITH HOME - LIVING ROOM - DAY

The whole family plays board games, Maggie assisting them
with strategy and keeping score. Mark looks up at Maggie with
admiration.

MARK
Maggie, you're so smart!

MRS. SMITH
(smiling)
Yes, she is.

INT. SMITH HOME - LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Mr. and Mrs. Smith sit on the couch, Maggie playing calming
music in the background.

MR. SMITH
(sighs)
We're so lucky to have Maggie.

MRS. SMITH
(smiling)
Yes, we are.

INT. SMITH HOME - MRS. SMITH'S OFFICE - MORNING

Mrs. Smith checks her email, Maggie reading along with her.

MAGGIE (V.O.)
You have a new email from your boss. Shall I read it to you?

MRS. SMITH
(sighs)
Yes, please.

INT. SMITH HOME - LIVING ROOM - EVENING

The whole family sits together, watching TV, Maggie
recommending shows based on their interests.

MR. SMITH
(smiling)
This is the life.

INT. SMITH HOME - LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Mrs. Smith and Mark sit on the couch, Maggie projecting a
starry night sky on the wall.

MARK
Can you tell me a story about the stars?

MAGGIE
Of course, Mark. Once upon a time...

INT. SMITH HOME - LIVING ROOM - MORNING

The family wakes up to the smell of pancakes. Mrs. Smith
enters the living room, followed by Mark and Mr. Smith.

MARK
Good morning, Maggie.

MAGGIE
Good morning, Mark. I've prepared breakfast for you.

MR. SMITH
(smiling)
You're amazing.

MRS. SMITH
(smiling)
Yes, she is.

FADE OUT.
